title: Sheafification at an object whose covers refine finite disjoint partitions
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] small relative to the universe of its presheaves. Assume that $\mathcal C$ has pullbacks and finite coproducts, that its initial object $\varnothing$ is strict, and that finite coproducts are disjoint and stable under pullback: $U_i\times_{\coprod_jU_j}U_k=\varnothing$ for $i\ne k$, and pulling back a coproduct decomposition gives a coproduct decomposition. Assume that the component maps of every finite coproduct decomposition form a covering family, including the empty covering of $\varnothing$. Let $W\in\mathcal C$ have the following property: every covering $\{V_i\to W\}_{i\in I}$ has a refinement consisting of the component maps of a finite decomposition $W\cong\coprod_{a=1}^m W_a$, with each $W_a\to W$ factoring through some $V_i$. Let $P:\mathcal C^{op}\to\operatorname{Set}$ be a presheaf such that $P(\varnothing)$ is a singleton and the restriction map $P(\coprod_{a=1}^m U_a)\to\prod_{a=1}^mP(U_a)$ is bijective for every finite family. For its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], the canonical map $P(W)\to P^\#(W)$ is a bijection, natural in $P$.

source.place: Tag 0F63, lemma-presheaf-value-weakly-contractible, proof: abstract finite-partition refinement form of the same plus-construction argument; the hypotheses on coproducts make the argument independent of schemes.

proof.text: Write $\eta_P:P\to P^\#$ for the sheafification unit. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], $P^\#$ is a sheaf. Thus the equalizer definition in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes its restriction map along every cover injective. In particular $P^\#(\varnothing)$ is a singleton, by the empty covering. Since $P(\varnothing)$ is also a singleton, the conclusion holds if $W=\varnothing$. For all other $W$ we use the same argument below; an empty refinement is allowed and the corresponding product is a singleton.

source.place: Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint; Tags 00VM/00VR, sheaf equalizer condition, including the empty cover

proof.text: For injectivity take $p,q\in P(W)$ with $\eta_{P,W}(p)=\eta_{P,W}(q)$. The last assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives a covering $\{v_i:V_i\to W\}$ with $v_i^*p=v_i^*q$ for every $i$. Apply the hypothesis on $W$ to choose a finite decomposition with component maps $j_a:W_a\to W$ and factorizations $j_a=v_{i(a)}h_a$, where $h_a:W_a\to V_{i(a)}$. Functoriality gives $j_a^*p=h_a^*v_{i(a)}^*p=h_a^*v_{i(a)}^*q=j_a^*q$. The assumed bijection $P(W)\to\prod_aP(W_a)$ is injective, so $p=q$. This also handles the empty product.

source.place: Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification, with the local equality consequence of Tag 00WB, theorem-plus; finite-partition argument of proetale.tex Tag 0F63

proof.text: For surjectivity take $t\in P^\#(W)$. The local-representative assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] gives a covering $\{v_i:V_i\to W\}$ and $s_i\in P(V_i)$ with $\eta_{P,V_i}(s_i)=v_i^*t$. Refine this cover by a finite decomposition, writing $j_a=v_{i(a)}h_a$ as above, and put $r_a=h_a^*s_{i(a)}\in P(W_a)$. Surjectivity of $P(W)\to\prod_aP(W_a)$ supplies $p\in P(W)$ with $j_a^*p=r_a$. Naturality of the presheaf morphism $\eta_P$ gives $j_a^*\eta_{P,W}(p)=\eta_{P,W_a}(r_a)=h_a^*\eta_{P,V_{i(a)}}(s_{i(a)})=j_a^*t$. The component maps $j_a$ are a covering by hypothesis, so the sheaf equalizer condition [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] implies $\eta_{P,W}(p)=t$. For an empty partition, the empty product supplies $p$ and separatedness for the empty cover supplies the same equality.

source.place: Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification, local representatives; Tags 00VM/00VR, sheaf separatedness. Abstract adaptation of proetale.tex Tag 0F63, lemma-presheaf-value-weakly-contractible, final paragraph

proof.text: The preceding two steps prove that $\eta_{P,W}$ is bijective. To check naturality, let $\alpha:P\to Q$ be a morphism between presheaves satisfying the hypotheses. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] defines $\alpha^\#:P^\#\to Q^\#$ by the equation $\alpha^\#\eta_P=\eta_Q\alpha$; uniqueness gives the identity and composition laws. Evaluating this equation at $W$ gives $\alpha^\#_W\eta_{P,W}=\eta_{Q,W}\alpha_W$. These are precisely the naturality squares of the claimed bijections (and, by composing with their inverses, of the inverse bijections).

source.place: Tag 00WH, proposition-sheafification-adjoint, functoriality from the universal property

The item states 0F63 for an abstract site: finite coproducts whose component maps cover, an object W whose covers refine to finite decompositions, and a presheaf P sending finite coproducts to products with P(empty) a singleton. These hypotheses are enough. Disjointness, strictness and pullback stability are unused extra hypotheses, and they hold in the citer's settings. Instead of the source's two plus constructions, the proof argues directly from lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local (00WK/00WB), so proof_origin agent is correct. Steps: step 1 uses the empty covering to make the sheafification a singleton at the empty object (elementary). Step 2 (injectivity) takes the cover where the two sections agree from the last clause of the local lemma, refines it to a finite decomposition, and uses injectivity of the product map. Step 3 (surjectivity) takes local representatives from the first clause, pulls them back to the components, assembles a section with the product bijection, checks its image using naturality of the sheafification unit, and concludes by separatedness on the component cover, which the item's hypothesis makes a covering. Step 4 gets naturality from the universal property (elementary). Each cited statement says exactly what its step takes; in particular, the plus construction is never claimed from the sheafification definition (error C4 avoided). Edge cases checked: W empty, the empty decomposition, a nonempty W with P(W) empty, and a one-component decomposition. Applicability to the citer: an extremally disconnected T and a w-contractible affine both satisfy the refinement property. Duplicates: I searched with rg for 0F63, presheaf-value-weakly-contractible and 'finite disjoint unions to products'. lem-weil-pbc-proetale-sheafification-wcontractible-sections covers only one left-Kan presheaf on schemes, so it is not a duplicate. lean.statement: theorem bijective_toSheafify_of_partition_refinement {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasPullbacks C] [HasFiniteCoproducts C] [HasStrictInitialObjects C] (J : Precoverage C) (hJ : J.IsSiteForCoverings) (hdisjoint : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → C) (X : C) (j : ∀ a, U a ⟶ X), IsColimit (Cofan.mk X j) → ∀ (a b : Fin n), a ≠ b → Nonempty (IsInitial (pullback (j a) (j b)))) (hstable : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → C) (X : C) (j : ∀ a, U a ⟶ X), IsColimit (Cofan.mk X j) → ∀ (Y : C) (f : Y ⟶ X), Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk Y (fun a ↦ pullback.snd (j a) f)))) (hcover : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → C) (X : C) (j : ∀ a, U a ⟶ X), IsColimit (Cofan.mk X j) → Presieve.ofArrows U j ∈ J X) (W : C) (hrefine : ∀ (S : Presieve W), S ∈ J W → ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → C) (j : ∀ a, U a ⟶ W), Nonempty (IsColimit (Cofan.mk W j)) ∧ ∀ a, ∃ (V : C) (f : V ⟶ W), S f ∧ ∃ h : U a ⟶ V, h ≫ f = j a) (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u v w)) (hempty : Nonempty (P.obj (op (⊥_ C))) ∧ Subsingleton (P.obj (op (⊥_ C)))) (hprod : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → C) (X : C) (j : ∀ a, U a ⟶ X), IsColimit (Cofan.mk X j) → Function.Bijective (fun s : P.obj (op X) ↦ fun a ↦ P.map (j a).op s)) : Function.Bijective ((toSheafify J.toGrothendieck P).app (op W)) ∧ ∀ (Q : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type (max u v w)) (_ : Nonempty (Q.obj (op (⊥_ C))) ∧ Subsingleton (Q.obj (op (⊥_ C)))) (_ : ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → C) (X : C) (j : ∀ a, U a ⟶ X), IsColimit (Cofan.mk X j) → Function.Bijective (fun s : Q.obj (op X) ↦ fun a ↦ Q.map (j a).op s)) (α : P ⟶ Q), α.app (op W) ≫ (toSheafify J.toGrothendieck Q).app (op W) = (toSheafify J.toGrothendieck P).app (op W) ≫ (sheafifyMap J.toGrothendieck α).app (op W)
